money_at_stake.basis: Searched for a dated figure sizing a spend, capex, or revenue pool that this specific occurrence, a No vote on reopening EU accession negotiations, itself moves. Found three adjacent figures and none of them qualifies. Iceland's own government revised, shortly before the vote, its official estimate of the annual net cost of full EU MEMBERSHIP: ISK 10 to 15 billion (about EUR 70 to 105 million), ISK 8 to 13 billion above current EEA-arrangement costs. That figure is explicitly the cost of eventual membership, and the referendum decided only whether to reopen negotiations toward it, not membership itself, so it is several steps removed from what this occurrence moves and the No result forecloses the whole path rather than triggering the number. The two capital programs press coverage places in the same North Atlantic security backdrop, a NATO fuel-storage expansion at Helguvik near Keflavik (up to about USD 67 million, NATO-financed per the reporting) and Denmark's new Greenland subsea cable (USD 468 million) inside its Arctic defense package, both predate the referendum and proceed on GIUK-gap and Danish Arctic-defense logic regardless of the vote's outcome; the Greenland cable reporting does not mention Iceland at all. This independently confirms Nell's own candidate-record basis, 'no published figure supports sizing that today.' SPECULATIVE is forbidden on this leg and no cited figure supports a band, so it is NULL rather than a reasoned guess.

evidence.claim: Iceland's government estimated its annual net contribution to the EU budget could be ISK 10 to 15 billion (about EUR 70 to 105 million), published in the final days before the referendum; the additional cost compared with Iceland's existing EEA arrangements would be ISK 8 to 13 billion (EUR 56 to 91 million) a year; and the referendum itself is not a vote on EU membership, only on whether to restart the accession negotiations suspended more than a decade ago.
evidence.source_name: NordiskPost, Iceland has changed how it calculates the cost of joining the EU
source_excerpt: Iceland's annual net contribution to the EU budget could be ISK 10–15 billion (€70–105 million)
the additional cost compared with the country's existing European Economic Area arrangements would be ISK 8–13 billion (€56–91 million) a year
The referendum is not a vote on EU membership itself. The question concerns whether Iceland should restart the negotiations suspended more than a decade ago.

evidence.claim: NATO is financing an expansion of the fuel storage facility being developed at Helguvik, about five miles from Keflavik International Airport, with the investment expected to total up to about USD 67 million according to the Icelandic daily Morgunbladid; the article does not mention Iceland's EU referendum or accession-talks debate at all.

source_excerpt: NATO is financing the construction, the statement said.

evidence.claim: Denmark's Arctic defense package added a new Greenland subsea cable at an estimated cost of DKK 3 billion (USD 468 million); Iceland is not mentioned anywhere in the article.
evidence.source_name: ArcticToday, New Greenlandic subsea cable worth 468 million added to Denmark's Arctic defense deal

public_reach.rationale: The one domestic issue this vote was actually fought over, fishing quota sovereignty, does include a single direct listed pure play: Brim hf. trades on the Main Market of Nasdaq Iceland under ticker BRIM as a fishing and fish-processing company. But quota ownership in that sector is heavily concentrated among a small number of groups: over the last decades 25 companies accumulated 75 percent of the fishing licenses, and the same reporting names Samherji, an international fishing group, among the handful of biggest fishing companies tied to that consolidation, so Brim is the exception rather than the rule even within the one sector this vote actually touches. And because the vote is a status-quo-preserving No rather than a change, it does not newly reallocate quota value toward or away from any of these names, listed or private. Iceland's whole listed market is small and thin regardless of sector: 27 companies on the Nasdaq Iceland Main Market plus 5 more on First North, EUR 24 billion combined market cap. On the Arctic-alignment side of the story, the concrete capital identified under money_at_stake, the Helguvik fuel facility and Denmark's Greenland cable, flows to NATO's own military construction budget and Danish state-linked infrastructure, not to a named public issuer surfaced in this search. Scored at the low end for a real but narrow and largely coincidental listed foothold, not because the domain is unreachable in principle.

capture_odds.basis: Capture requires a specific link or issuer whose margin is at stake. None has been established: the vote preserves rather than changes the status quo on the one domestic issue, fishing quota sovereignty, it was fought over, and the Arctic-security capital identified under money_at_stake (Helguvik, the Greenland cable) is not tied to this occurrence's outcome. Scoring a capture number here would mean guessing which downstream link, if any, is actually moved by North Atlantic realignment following this vote, which is a chain-build question and out of scope for a pre-chain appraisal.

timing_fit.basis: Timing_fit measures whether the money moves inside 2 to 5 years; with no money pool established under money_at_stake, there is nothing dated to time. A citation this appraisal originally carried for a Prime Ministerial statement bounding the political question through 2028 did not hold up: the cited CNBC URL does not contain that quote (confirmed by re-fetching it and by an adversarial verifier's independent fetch of the same page), so that evidence item is removed rather than repaired with a different source. What remains is a plain absence: no dated capital plan ties any investable spend to this referendum's outcome, so the leg is recorded as NULL rather than stretched into a score.

unranked_reason: money_at_stake, capture_odds and timing_fit are NULL. This occurrence is a referendum result that decided only whether Iceland would reopen EU accession negotiations, and it decided no. No dated source, official or press, sizes a spend, capex, or revenue pool that this specific result itself moves: Iceland's own government estimate of EU-membership cost (ISK 10 to 15 billion a year) is explicitly the cost of eventual membership, several steps beyond a vote on reopening talks, and the Arctic-security capital programs found nearby (the Helguvik NATO fuel facility, Denmark's Greenland subsea cable) predate the vote and are not caused by its outcome. Absent a sized pool, capture_odds and timing_fit have no chain-specific subject to score against. public_reach is the one leg with an independently gradable structural answer, scored 30 on Brim hf.'s status as a genuine but narrow listed pure play inside an otherwise concentrated and status-quo-preserved domestic sector.

notes.text: The occurrence claim itself was independently verified this run, not just taken from Nell's campaign_record. WebSearch this run corroborates the exact figures (52.8 percent against, 47.2 percent for, 82.5 percent turnout) across CNBC (Nell's own cited source), ABC News Australia, Al Jazeera, Euronews and NPR, all dated 2026-08-30 or the overnight count on 2026-08-29 to 2026-08-30. The occurrence stands as reported.

UNRANKED is not a statement that this occurrence is unimportant, only that nobody, including this appraisal, has published a number tying an investable pool to it. Nell's own candidate record already flagged this as an ALTERNATE included specifically to keep the campaign's denominator honest (economic_impact 30, public_market_reach 35, disposition ALTERNATE), and this appraisal's independent research reaches the same place from the money side: real domestic economics exist (fishing quota concentration, a government EU-cost estimate) but none of it is caused by this occurrence or lands on a chain a brokerage account can buy. If a future event ties a dated capital program directly to this referendum's outcome, for example a specific North Atlantic basing or infrastructure commitment made because Iceland stayed outside the EU, this appraisal should be amended rather than recreated.

Source_excerpt pass (method section 1, 2026-08-30 rule): every cited URL in this appraisal was re-fetched this run. Six items had their claim confirmed verbatim and were upgraded to VERIFIED with a quoted source_excerpt attached (the two Wikipedia pages, ftm.eu, NordiskPost, Stars and Stripes, ArcticToday). One item, timing_fit's CNBC citation for a Prime Ministerial 2028-mandate quote, did not hold up: the cited URL does not contain that quote on refetch, so the item was deleted rather than repaired with a substitute source, per this pass's explicit rule against reaching for a new source to save a claim. The ftm.eu claim was also trimmed: its original wording asserted Samherji is 'privately held' and is the sector's 'largest name,' neither of which the source states; the claim now states only what the source verbatim supports. No leg's score or band changed as a result (money_at_stake, capture_odds and timing_fit were already NULL; public_reach's evidentiary support strengthened without changing its 30 score).

Excerpt-repair pass, requested as a targeted fix for three evidence items that reportedly carried no source_excerpt. On inspection, all three were the 'Tally appraisal search, <leg> ...' entries tagged NULL in money_at_stake, capture_odds and timing_fit: recorded absences (searches that found nothing), carrying no URL and no external source to fetch or quote. Both tools/check_impact.py (check_corpus_excerpts skips e.get('tag') == 'NULL' and skips a leg entirely when the leg itself is NULL) and tools/validate.py (check_evidence: 'a NULL is a recorded absence; it has nothing to cite') exempt this exact shape by design, and an empirical run of check_corpus_excerpts against this file before this pass returned zero findings. Fetching a source for a claim that is 'nothing was found' is not possible without fabricating one, which is the defect this whole repair pass exists to avoid. Rather than leave a redundant item that looks unsourced to a future reader (which is exactly the confusion that produced this repair request), the three NULL-tag search-log items are deleted; the full search rationale they summarized remains in each leg's own basis field, unchanged. Zero URLs were fetched this pass because none of the three flagged items named a fetchable source. No leg's score, band, or basis changed: money_at_stake, capture_odds and timing_fit remain correctly NULL, and this occurrence remains UNRANKED for the same stated reasons.
